BLINDSPOT_2_Exhibit_Data_Consistency.description: D-Program has 0 exhibits across all 15 cases (closure report M2). ENHANCED_CASE_BASE has 1-2 exhibits per case with rich data. Must verify: numbers in exhibits are internally consistent, every exhibit row is consumed by at least one item, subtotals add up.
BLINDSPOT_2_Exhibit_Data_Consistency.risk: Exhibit data errors were never caught in D-Program because D-Program has no exhibits. This is a new risk class for BASE.

BLINDSPOT_3_CrossCase_Domain_Coverage.description: D-Program covered all 6 blueprint domains (A-F). BASE already covers A-F. Verify no domain gaps and no inter-domain topic repeats within the same case.

BLINDSPOT_4_Explanation_Wave_Drift.description: D-Program Wave 1 had shorter explanations (500-677 chars) vs. Wave 5 (1,612-2,055 chars). This quality gradient means early waves were certified at a lower standard. BASE should set an explicit quality floor that ALL waves must meet.
BLINDSPOT_4_Explanation_Wave_Drift.risk: Wave-1-certified items may pass with minimal expansion while Wave-5 items receive much more thorough treatment. Learners see inconsistent quality.
BLINDSPOT_4_Explanation_Wave_Drift.recommendation: Enforce a minimum 500-char explanation floor for ALL items, regardless of wave. Apply retroactive review to Wave 1 cases if needed.

BLINDSPOT_5_CognitiveLevel_Distribution.description: D-Program has 61% Understand vs. 15% CAQS target. CBQ5 has similar heavy Understand concentration. BASE, with its Apply/Evaluate mix, may provide better distribution — but should be verified before certification.
BLINDSPOT_5_CognitiveLevel_Distribution.risk: If BASE items are certified with accurate CognitiveLevel assignments but poor distribution, the overall pool still fails CAQS §6.2 psychometric targets.

BLINDSPOT_6_Difficulty_Recalibration_Def.description: D-Program Wave 1 difficulty was recalibrated post-hoc (closure report C2). BASE should calibrate difficulty BEFORE certification to avoid retroactive changes on Certified items.
BLINDSPOT_6_Difficulty_Recalibration_Def.risk: Certifying items with wrong difficulty and fixing later creates governance-guard Rule 4 (answer-key change) alert cascade and REVISION_HISTORY overhead.

BLINDSPOT_7_Backup_Protocol_Compliance.description: D-Program had 2 backup protocol violations (S525/S526 files in root, not backups/). BASE certification sessions must pre-verify backup paths.
BLINDSPOT_7_Backup_Protocol_Compliance.risk: Root-level .bak files violate PROJECT_CONSTITUTION.md §11.4. Cumulative governance debt.

BLINDSPOT_8_ProductionStatus_Promotion.description: D-Program has CASE-D1/D2/D3 ProductionStatus: 'Draft' despite question_state: 'Certified' (closure report H1). BASE should promote ProductionStatus to 'Production' as part of each certification wave.
BLINDSPOT_8_ProductionStatus_Promotion.risk: Inconsistent ProductionStatus after certification is a metadata hygiene issue that requires a separate remediation session.

KEY_FINDINGS: ENHANCED_CASE_BASE is the ONLY remaining uncertified case-bank array (0/90 Certified). All four prior programs are 100% Certified.
Explanation quality gap is the largest deficiency: ~96 chars avg vs. D-Program post-certification 1,282 chars. Requires 8-13x expansion.
ENHANCED_CASE_BASE has richer exhibit data (1-2 per case) than D-Program (0 exhibits), making it pedagogically superior but requiring additional exhibit-data-consistency verification.
No DL-008/DL-016/DL-029 risk — case-study single-block architecture means MCQ-specific defect categories do not apply. This simplifies the certification pipeline.
Difficulty inflation (DL-031) is systematic: most items labeled Moderate(3) but testing at Apply(2) level with simple arithmetic. Recalibrate BEFORE certification to avoid post-hoc fixes.
Prior programs show quality gradient across waves (D-Program W1: 500-677 → W5: 1,612-2,055). BASE should enforce a uniform quality floor across all waves.

ENHANCED_CASE_BASE metadata is more complete than pre-certification D-Program items (already has CognitiveLevel, DifficultyDrivers, CalculationComplexity, etc.). Metadata enrichment workload is lower than D-Program.
ENHANCED_CASE_BASE has 6 items/case vs. 5 in prior programs — certification workload is ~20% higher per case (7.5 cases @ 6 vs. 9 cases @ 5 for 90 items).

CBQ2 certification standard (short explanations, minimal expansion) represents the lowest acceptable floor. D-Program standard (1,282 avg, detailed) represents the quality ceiling. BASE should target at least CBQ4 quality level.

Critical pre-certification step not done in prior programs: independent answer-key verification BEFORE any certification waves. DL-030 (5 wrong CCs in MCQ pool) demonstrates why this must be front-loaded.
RECOMMENDED_EXECUTION_ORDER: Step 0 (Pre-Wave): Independent answer-key audit — recalculate all 30-40 numeric items from exhibit data. Flag any mismatches.
Step 0b (Pre-Wave): Difficulty calibration — reassign Difficulty/DifficultyScore for all 90 items to match CognitiveLevel and actual complexity.
Step 1: W1 — Cases CBQ-A1/A2/A3 (Section A, 18 items): Expand explanations to 500+ chars, add ASC/COSO citations, business interpretation, distractor rationale.
Step 2: W2 — Cases CBQ-B1/B2/B3 (Section B, 18 items)
Step 3: W3 — Cases CBQ-C1/C2/C3 (Section C, 18 items)
Step 4: W4 — Cases CBQ-D1/D2 + CBQ-E1/E2 (Sections D+E, 24 items or split into two sessions)
Step 5: W5 — Cases CBQ-F1/F2 (Section F, 12 items)
Step 6: Governance Closeout (all 90 items): Cross-wave quality consistency audit, ProductionStatus promotion, RevisionHistory consolidation, backup compliance check.
Each wave: backup-before-write, ≤30 items per governance-guard Rule 5, independent post-wave verification.
EXPECTED_CHALLENGES: CHALLENGE 1 — Time Per Item: Writing 500-1,200 char explanations with ASC citations, trap warnings, and distractor rationale for 90 items will require significant session time. D-Program consumed 5 sessions for 75 items at 15 items/wave. At 18 items/wave, expect 90 minutes+ per wave.

CHALLENGE 2 — Quality Consistency Across Waves: Prior programs showed quality improvement across waves (later waves had better explanations). Must enforce uniform minimum-char-per-explanation floor and consistent citation style.
CHALLENGE 3 — Exhibit Data Verification: 15 CBQ cases have ~25 exhibits with varying data. Verify numerical consistency across all exhibit rows before certifying items that depend on them.

CHALLENGE 4 — Difficulty Calibration Pre-Wave: Recalibrating 90 items before starting waves is a separate workload. Without it, items will be certified with inflated difficulty — same as D-Program Wave 1 issue.

CHALLENGE 5 — 6-Item Cases: ENHANCED_CASE_BASE has 6 items/case vs. 5 in prior programs. Extra item per case means ~20% more work per case. 18-item waves may need splitting to 2 cases (12 items) per session.
CHALLENGE 6 — No ExplanationWrong Fields: All distractor rationale must go inline in the Explanation field. The rendering engine must be verified to handle this correctly for case-study items.

CHALLENGE 7 — Legacy CASE-* Items in Same File: scored_cases.js also contains 15 legacy cases (CASE-A1, CASE-B1, etc.) totaling 120 items. The CBQ cases share the same ENHANCED_CASE_BASE array. Care must be taken to ONLY modify CBQ-* items and leave legacy items untouched.
CHALLENGE 8 — Backup Protocol for Large File: scored_cases.js is 8,512 lines (~380KB). Each backup copy is ~380KB. 6 waves = ~2.3MB of backup files. Ensure backups/ directory has adequate space.
